title: Console: experiment creation wizard + guardrail configuration (Route Experiments)
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Overview
- This ticket designs the end-to-end Console flow for creating a route-level experiment (A/B/n) and configuring guardrails (latency/cost/error + optional quality signals). Scope includes: wizard IA, interaction patterns, validation UX, empty states, and RBAC-aware affordances.
- This is the primary user-facing workflow for Phase 2 (Console workflow + dashboards) and is a dependency for beta onboarding and docs.

Primary personas
- Platform Engineer: wants deterministic routing, safe controls, clear blast radius, and fast rollback.
- ML Engineer / Applied ML: wants variant comparisons and optional quality guardrails (eval scores).

Goals
1) Enable a safe, guided creation flow for route experiments with clear defaults and guardrails.
2) Make advanced concepts (stickiness, traffic splits, precedence with rollouts/fallback) understandable without reading docs.
3) Reduce misconfiguration by pushing validation earlier (inline) and blocking only when necessary.
4) Ensure guardrails are easy to configure with sensible defaults and explicit semantics (soft-stop vs hard-stop).

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Statistical significance UI (beyond basic deltas and guardrail status in results view).
- Custom metric ingestion UI.

Proposed wizard information architecture (current)
Step 1: Basics
- Fields: Experiment name, optional description, owner team (optional), duration (optional, for reminders only).
- Note: we explicitly avoid "end date = auto stop" semantics in beta; stop remains an explicit action.

Step 2: Route + eligibility
- Select route (dropdown/search). Display normalized route identifier (template) with a tooltip explaining cardinality reasons.
- Optional eligibility rules (advanced): region allowlist, account tier constraints, request attribute filters.
- Copy highlights precedence: "Experiments are evaluated during routing before fallback policies" (matches current routing order).

Step 3: Variants
- Add 2–4 variants (GA target max TBD; design currently supports up to 5 but recommends 2–3).
- For each variant:
  - Variant name (A, B, C… default)
  - Model target selector (model + version) OR policy target (if variant points to an existing rollout target)
  - Optional notes
- Inline compatibility warning (non-blocking unless hard incompatible): model architecture mismatch, unsupported tool-calling mode, etc. (driven by backend validation; UI surfaces in place).

Step 4: Traffic split + stickiness
- Split control: percentage inputs with slider affordance; sum must equal 100.
- Default: 50/50 for 2 variants.
- Stickiness key (required to avoid skew):
  - Recommended default shown first: customer-provided stable key (e.g., end_user_id / session_id / customer_id).
  - Allow selecting precedence order (e.g., explicit header > customer_id > end_user_id > session_id).
  - Show warning if selection could be low entropy (e.g., missing header fallback to IP hash). Copy: "Low-entropy keys can cause variant skew and misleading results."
- Determinism helper: show a read-only "assignment preview" example using a sample key to explain determinism at a high level.

Step 5: Guardrails
- Toggle: "Enable guardrails" (on by default).
- Guardrail categories:
  - Latency: p95, p99 thresholds relative to baseline (control) OR absolute SLO threshold. Default mode: relative delta.
  - Errors: error rate delta threshold.
  - Cost: cost/token delta threshold (requires attribution pipeline).
  - Quality (optional / beta): available if eval streams enabled for account; otherwise show disabled state with link to enablement.
- Semantics (aligned with PM + SRE decision):
  - Default behavior: Soft-stop (mark experiment degraded, notify, surface banner in Console).
  - Optional behavior (behind advanced toggle / later beta): Auto-stop (hard stop) with kill switch. UI shows this as "Stop experiment automatically" with explicit confirmation copy.
- UX components:
  - Defaults are prefilled; user can edit.
  - Each guardrail row includes: metric selector, threshold input, evaluation window selector (e.g., 5m/15m/1h), and severity label.
  - Banner text preview (what on-call / operators will see) to reduce surprise.

Step 6: Review + confirm
- Summary page: route, variants, split, stickiness, guardrails, audit implications.
- Strong callout: "Starting an experiment will immediately begin routing traffic according to the split." (If we support "Create as Draft", show both actions.)
- Actions:
  - "Create draft" (recommended default)
  - "Create and start" (requires elevated permission)

RBAC-aware affordances
- Read-only users:
  - Can view wizard summary but cannot submit. Primary CTA disabled with tooltip: "You do not have permission to create experiments."
- Create permission but not start:
  - Can "Create draft" only; "Create and start" hidden or disabled based on product decision (currently: disabled with tooltip).
- Stop permission:
  - Not in this ticket directly, but copy and state patterns for start/stop are aligned with DES-322.

Validation & error states (UX)
- Blockers:
  - Traffic split sum != 100
  - Only 1 variant
  - Missing stickiness configuration
  - Backend validation errors: overlapping active experiment on same route (policy decision in progress), model incompatibility hard failures, invalid eligibility rules.
- Warnings (non-blocking):
  - Low entropy stickiness fallback
  - Very small split (< 5%) with note: "Metrics may be noisy; consider larger split for faster guardrail confidence."
  - Guardrails disabled (requires explicit checkbox acknowledgement)

Open questions
1) Overlapping experiments on same route
- Current proposal: disallow overlapping active experiments on the same route by default; allow override only for internal users (or later). Needs final product decision + backend behavior.

2) Baseline definition for deltas
- Proposal: baseline = control variant (Variant A) unless user designates a different baseline. UI should allow selecting the baseline variant in Step 3 or Step 5.

3) Guardrail evaluation windows + rollup latency
- Need to ensure UI copy accurately sets expectations (e.g., "metrics update within ~2–5 minutes" depending on aggregation). Avoid promising real-time.

4) Quality guardrails availability
- If eval streams not enabled: show disabled section with a short explanation + link to enablement. Confirm enablement trigger and messaging with Applied ML (Maya/Jonas).

Design review feedback (iterative)
- 2025-01-22 (PM Marissa Cole): requested "Create as Draft" to be the happy path to avoid accidental starts; add clearer summary before start.
- 2025-01-24 (Eng Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin): asked to surface server-side validation errors inline per step rather than a single error toast on submit; prefer an "error summary" at top + field-level anchors.
- 2025-01-28 (SRE Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes): pushed for explicit soft-stop vs auto-stop labeling and an acknowledgment for auto-stop; requested links to runbooks in degraded banners (handled in results view but we added banner preview copy here).
- 2025-02-03 (Telemetry Logan Wright): flagged metric cardinality concerns; asked to avoid selecting arbitrary route strings and to display normalized route templates by default (updated Step 2).
- 2025-02-07 (Support feedback relayed via Console team): customers confused by variant headers; add tooltip in Step 6 explaining how to debug assignment (variant header names, where to look). This will be mirrored in docs.

Deliverables
- Figma prototypes for:
  - Full wizard flow (draft + start)
  - Guardrails configuration interactions and states (disabled, warning, degraded preview)
  - RBAC disabled states
  - Inline validation and error summary patterns
- UX copy snippets for:
  - Stickiness explanations
  - Guardrail semantics
  - Draft vs start
- Handoff notes to ENG-9025 (UI implementation) including component inventory.

Acceptance criteria
- Creation wizard supports: route selection, 2+ variants, traffic split, stickiness key choice, guardrail configuration, review step.
- All blocking validations are shown before submit; server-side errors map to the relevant step.
- RBAC states are defined for create/start permissions and are consistent across the wizard.
- Copy and semantics match agreed guardrail behavior (soft-stop default; auto-stop explicitly opt-in).

Next steps
- Finalize open question #1 (overlapping active experiments) with PM + policy engine constraints.
- Design QA with ENG-9025 once implemented behind feature flag.
- Ensure alignment with DES-322 (results dashboard) for shared terminology (variant, baseline, degraded, stopped).

Changelog
- v3 (2025-02-21): Added baseline selector, normalized route display, and auto-stop confirmation copy.
- v2 (2025-02-07): Added draft as default action, improved stickiness guidance, added warnings for low split sizes.
- v1 (2025-01-15): Initial wireframes + step structure.
